name: open-badges
label: Open Badges / Verifiable Credentials
description: W3C digital credentials — professional development, micro-credentials, certificates

table_notes.ob_issuer: Organisations or individuals authorised to award badges; each badge class traces back to one issuer for provenance.
table_notes.ob_badge_class: The badge definition (template): what it represents, how it is earned, and optional alignment to external frameworks such as O*NET or CASE.
table_notes.ob_assertion: A single awarded badge — ties one recipient to one badge class with evidence, issuance date, and revocation state.
table_notes.ob_endorsement: A third-party claim by an issuer attesting that a specific assertion is credible or high-quality.

ob_issuer.name: id
ob_issuer.description: Unique identifier for the issuing organisation or individual

ob_issuer.name: name
ob_issuer.description: Legal or display name of the issuing entity

ob_issuer.name: url
ob_issuer.description: Canonical homepage URL of the issuer for public verification

ob_issuer.name: email
ob_issuer.description: Contact email for the issuer (RFC 5321 max length)

ob_issuer.name: description
ob_issuer.description: Human-readable description of the issuing organisation and its mission

ob_issuer.name: image_url
ob_issuer.description: URL to the issuer's logo or branding image displayed on badges

ob_issuer.name: public_key
ob_issuer.description: PEM-encoded public key used to cryptographically sign assertions (OB 3.0 JWS)

ob_badge_class.name: id
ob_badge_class.description: Unique identifier for this badge class definition

ob_badge_class.name: issuer_id
ob_badge_class.description: References ob_issuer — the organisation that owns and awards this badge

ob_badge_class.name: name
ob_badge_class.description: Human-readable title of the badge (e.g. 'Python Fundamentals Certificate')

ob_badge_class.name: description
ob_badge_class.description: What the badge represents and what the earner accomplished

ob_badge_class.name: image_url
ob_badge_class.description: URL to the visual badge image shown to recipients and on profiles

ob_badge_class.name: criteria_narrative
ob_badge_class.description: Plain-text description of the requirements that must be met to earn this badge

ob_badge_class.name: criteria_url
ob_badge_class.description: URL to the full criteria page hosted by the issuer

ob_badge_class.name: alignment
ob_badge_class.description: JSONB array of alignment objects linking badge to external frameworks (O*NET, CASE, CTDL)

ob_badge_class.name: tags
ob_badge_class.description: JSON array of keyword strings for discovery and filtering (e.g. ["python", "data"])

ob_badge_class.name: created_at
ob_badge_class.description: Timestamp when this badge class was first created

ob_assertion.name: id
ob_assertion.description: Unique identifier for this awarded badge instance

ob_assertion.name: badge_class_id
ob_assertion.description: References ob_badge_class — the definition being awarded

ob_assertion.name: recipient_id
ob_assertion.description: Identifier for the recipient — typically an email address or hashed email

ob_assertion.name: issued_on
ob_assertion.description: Date the badge was officially awarded to the recipient

ob_assertion.name: expires_on
ob_assertion.description: Optional expiry date after which the badge is no longer considered valid

ob_assertion.name: evidence_url
ob_assertion.description: URL to evidence (portfolio item, project, exam result) supporting this award

ob_assertion.name: narrative
ob_assertion.description: Free-text description of how this specific recipient earned the badge

ob_assertion.name: verification_type
ob_assertion.description: Coding: how the assertion can be verified — 'HostedBadge', 'SignedBadge', or 'JWS'

ob_assertion.name: revoked
ob_assertion.description: True if the issuer has revoked this badge (e.g. due to fraud or error)

ob_assertion.name: revocation_reason
ob_assertion.description: Human-readable explanation of why the badge was revoked; NULL if not revoked

ob_endorsement.name: id
ob_endorsement.description: Unique identifier for this endorsement record

ob_endorsement.name: assertion_id
ob_endorsement.description: References ob_assertion — the specific awarded badge being endorsed

ob_endorsement.name: issuer_id
ob_endorsement.description: References ob_issuer — the third party making the endorsement claim

ob_endorsement.name: claim
ob_endorsement.description: The endorsing party's written statement about the quality or validity of this badge

short_description: W3C digital credentials — professional development, micro-credentials, certificates
long_description: Open Badges 3.0 is the W3C Verifiable Credentials-based standard for digital credentials. The schema covers the complete badge lifecycle: issuer identity, badge class definitions (criteria, alignment to standards), assertions (issued badges with recipient), and endorsements from third parties verifying badge quality.
when_to_use: Use for professional development platforms, certification systems, workforce development tools, or any app that issues verifiable digital credentials. Adopted by LinkedIn, Acclaim, Credly, and major certification bodies. Required for compliance with US workforce development grants that mandate portable credentials. Growing adoption in EU Digital Credentials for Learning.
